## Snowdrop — *Silly Filly Studios*

Snowdrop is the blind, pale-blue pegasus filly at the center of Silly Filly Studios' 2013 fan short *Snowdrop*. In ancient Cloudsdale, she invents the delicate snowflake and convinces Equestria that winter can be beautiful, too. Her friendship with Princess Luna—and Luna's farewell over a thousand years later—is the film's emotional heart. This is her own fan-film continuity, not an appearance in Hasbro's *Friendship Is Magic* television canon.

[![Snowdrop with Luna and Celestia — original film artwork, SFS Animation](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/do6RDSwaWek/maxresdefault.jpg)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=do6RDSwaWek)

*Original production image: SFS Animation.*

### Recognition, name, and appearances

Her pale icy-blue coat, curled white mane and tail with cyan streaks, light-blue eyes, and eventual snowflake-on-a-stem cutie mark make her distinctive. The studio already used **Snowdrop** in its [September 2012 trailer](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SStVMfJeyF0): it is a creator-assigned name, not a later fandom label for a TV background pony. She speaks extensively in the March 21, 2013 short, voiced by **Meredith Sims** (credited as **Emichwan88**); her mother is **Primrose**. The [character record](https://mlpfanart.fandom.com/wiki/Snowdrop_%28character%29) documents her look and original voice credit.

In *Friendship is Witchcraft* episode 9, *Seed No Evil* (2013), Sherclop Pones repurposes the character and footage as **Snowblind**, voiced by Jenny Nicholson. Snowblind is a **parody reinterpretation**, not Snowdrop's secret identity or an official TV appearance; see the [parody episode's account](https://mlpfanart.fandom.com/wiki/Seed_No_Evil). Other depictions are fan works; no official G4 episode, film, or comic appearance was verified.

## Important moments

All four scenes occur in *Snowdrop* (2013), a standalone fan short with **no season/episode numbering**. The official full film is linked through the production image above; **exact scene timestamps were not independently verified**.

1. **An outsider at school** — Snowdrop's classmates dismiss winter and doubt her ability to contribute, establishing why she longs to prove herself.
2. **Hearing the stars** — Primrose's encouragement helps Snowdrop recognize the twinkling sound of snow and fashion her first star-shaped snowflake.
3. **A star for winter** — At the Spring Sunrise presentation, Snowdrop defends her handmade “wishing snow” before Celestia and Luna; the princesses ask her to make more.
4. **Luna's last snowflake** — Over a millennium later, Luna reluctantly releases Snowdrop's last surviving flake in tribute to the friend who understood her night.
